To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the number of citations to cardiovascular clinical trials published in three major medical journals was significantly higher for trials funded by the pharmaceutical industry than for trials funded by other sources, and (2) this difference in the number of citations was most striking in trials of drugs in which the new treatment was favored over standard care, but was less striking for trials in which the drug was not favored over standard care.
